slot.brief: Aldohexose undergoes Kiliani–Fischer chain extension; ask how many stereoisomeric products form, which pairs are epimers/diastereomers, and which are optically active — demanding stereo-reasoning.

stem: An optically active aldohexose undergoes Kiliani–Fischer chain extension in its open-chain form, with its existing stereocentres retained. Which statement about the aldoheptose products is correct?
options: Two products; C-2 epimers and diastereomers; both are optically active.
Two products; enantiomers; both are optically active.
Four products; two pairs of C-2 epimers; all are optically active.
Two products; C-7 epimers; both are optically inactive.

verdicts.working: Kiliani–Fischer extension creates a new stereocentre at C-2. Its two configurations give C-2 epimers; the retained stereocentres make them diastereomers, and both products are chiral.

working:
One new stereocentre at C-2 gives $2$ products; the existing centres are unchanged. Inversion only at C-2 gives epimers (hence diastereomers). Both retain chiral centres and are optically active.

Independent check: Kiliani–Fischer extension creates a new stereocentre at C-2. Its two configurations give C-2 epimers; the retained stereocentres make them diastereomers, and both products are chiral.
solution: Kiliani–Fischer extension creates one new stereocentre at C-2, giving $2$ products while retaining the original stereocentres. They differ only at C-2, so they are epimers and hence diastereomers; both remain optically active.
